Dear Members,
when I did a pathmodell with one latent variable and my endogenous variables are not kategorical, it works in lavaan. At a next step, I transformed one endogenous non kategorical variable in a 0/1-categorical variable. I run the procedure again and told lavaan in the sem-function with the "ordered"-command , that one endogenous variable ("va01_dummy") is a categorical variable. It didn't work and lavaan gave me an error-feddback (see below). What  is the problem? I suppose  it has something to do with characteristic and double variables!


s4_ex9 <- '
# Latent variables
Ordnung =~ 1*va01_dummy
Ausländer=~1*ma02 + ma03+ ma04


# Regressions
va01_dummy~ year + lp01 + lp02
Ausländer ~ va01_dummy + year + lp01 + lp02
 

# Variances
Ordnung ~~Ordnung + Ausländer
Ausländer ~~ Ausländer 


# Covariances
year~~lp01 + lp02
lp01 ~~ lp02


#Fehlervarianzen
va01_dummy ~~ 0.3252*va01_dummy
'
str(allbus_dat)
# Fit the model 
s4_ex9_unc_fit <- sem( s4_ex9, data = allbus_dat, group = 'eastwest_re', 
                       estimator= "WLSMV", meanstructure = FALSE, 
                       ordered="va01_dummy")

messages.subject: Re: error-Interpretation
parts:
What  is the problem?

Not sure, but it looks like it has something to do with ...
I suppose  it has something to do with characteristic and double variables!

oh, right.  Maybe the way you calculated the dummy code didn't result in a numeric/integer class variable.  Try inspecting your data.frame's contents with str() or summary(), or class(allbus_dat$va01_dummy) for example.  I usually use ifelse(..., 1, 0) to create dummy codes.

Some other problems with your syntax:

s4_ex9 <- '

# Latent variables
Ordnung =~ 1*va01_dummy

# Variances
Ordnung ~~Ordnung
#Fehlervarianzen
va01_dummy ~~ 0.3252*va01_dummy
'

A single continuous indicator of a construct requires the fixed loading and residual variance, as your syntax does.  But the latent response underlying va01_dummy is not estimable and would be fixed already by default, so there is no observed variance to "put into the latent space" of its factor.  Given the default delta parameterization, marginal variances are fixed to 1.  So you can identify the model by fixing the Ordnung variance to the indicator's assumed reliability and fix va01_dummy's residual variance to 1 minus reliability (presumably what you did here).

s4_ex9_unc_fit <- sem( s4_ex9, data = allbus_dat, group = 'eastwest_re', 
                       estimator= "WLSMV", meanstructure = FALSE, 
                       ordered="va01_dummy")

You cannot set meanstructure=FALSE when you have categorical data.  Their mean and covariance structures both depend on the threshold model.
